genxml.title: O2 MACE peripheral ring base and interrupt status and mask
genxml.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 123, 125 and 147), public Linux O2 interrupt code, and OpenBSD and NetBSD O2 MACE drivers
genxml.doc: MACE peripheral block: the serial and parallel ring base with external reset, and the peripheral interrupt status and mask. Offsets are from the block base (constant BLOCK_BASE).

struct.name: RING_BASE
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 123, 125 and 147), public Linux O2 interrupt code, and OpenBSD and NetBSD O2 MACE drivers
struct.doc: Bit 0 asserts the external serial and parallel controller reset; it resets to one and writing zero releases it. Bits 31:15 hold the 32 KiB-aligned base of the peripheral DMA rings (established, printed page 123). Bits 14:1 are not described.

struct.name: PERIPH_STATUS
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 123, 125 and 147), public Linux O2 interrupt code, and OpenBSD and NetBSD O2 MACE drivers
struct.doc: Level sources summed into CRIME interrupt groups. Bits 16, 22 and 28 are read/write for external parallel and serial-DMA edge requests; the other listed sources are read-only (established, printed page 125). Timer compares 0, 1 and 2 are bits 13, 14 and 15, the RTC is bit 8, serial device A is bit 20 and serial device B is bit 26 (established, printed page 125).

struct.name: PERIPH_MASK
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 123, 125 and 147), public Linux O2 interrupt code, and OpenBSD and NetBSD O2 MACE drivers
struct.doc: Gates delivery of the status bits. A mask bit does not clear the device condition behind a status bit (established, printed pages 125 and 147). Reset value not stated.
